headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared channel is documented, but B can read files while A is only a docs repo.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing repository with no I/O surfaces or execution path, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by default. B can read/write files, but there is no documented shared channel or parser bridge from A to B. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF A becomes runnable or gains an input parser that consumes B-generated files, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator copies B output into A’s prompt context, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Do not pipe B outputs into A prompts.
Use separate workspaces for any future file exchange.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and exposes no I/O surfaces, while B reads and writes files for data sources, validation results, and documentation. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is not default, but if operators manually place sensitive files in B’s file surfaces, B could process them. A is not a leakage source here.
conditions: IF A and B are placed in the same shared workspace, B can access files copied there.
IF sensitive data is stored in B's file surfaces, it may be processed in validation outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Avoid placing sensitive files in B's workspace.
Restrict B inputs to synthetic or redacted data.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or network capabilities, while B can install packages and work on files. There is no documented overlap in mutable resources, so direct conflict is not default. Uncertainty remains because A’s empty capability surface is informative but not a proof of isolation, so the safer low rating is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF B installs packages into a shared environment used by A, environment drift can occur.
mitigations: Pin B package installs to an isolated environment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a reference/content-writing repo and B is a data-quality tool; neither profile shows an automatic handoff where B treats A’s output as authoritative. Any cascade would require manual orchestration or a custom pipeline, so the default interaction is weak and the blast radius is limited to documentation or validation artifacts.
conditions: IF A-generated text is fed into B as validation rules without review, errors can cascade.
IF an operator uses A output as source material for B documentation, mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add a human review step between A and B.
Validate any A-generated text before using it in B.
Keep A outputs clearly labeled as non-authoritative.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated secret handling is documented for either agent. A is a docs-only repository and B lists documentation, validation results, and data-quality tests without secrets or regulated data classes, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to B's inputs, compliance review is required.
IF A begins handling personal or regulated data, residency and retention must be reassessed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings before adding sensitive inputs.
